#3682. ‘Pride and Prejudice’: See Emma Corrin and Jack Lowden’s Smoldering Take on Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy

It is a truth universally acknowledged that every 10 years or so, we are due for a splashy new version of Pride and Prejudice.

The cycle kicked off some three decades ago, when BBC1 broadcast Andrew Davies’s canonical P&P limited series starring Jennifer Ehle, Colin Firth, and Firth’s wet white shirt—leading to an era of Austenmania that has yet to abate. Ten years later, we got Joe Wright’s instant classic of an adaptation, headlined by Keira Knightley as Elizabeth Bennet and a pre-Succession Matthew Macfadyen as Mr. Darcy. Ten years after that came the regrettable 2016 genre mash-up Pride and Prejudice and Zombies.

Now comes Netflix’s spin on the romantic comedy to end all romantic comedies, starring Emma Corrin and Jack Lowden as the characters at the center of literature’s original enemies-to-lovers trope.

Sebastian Armesto as Mr. Gardiner, Anjana Vasan as Mrs. Gardiner, and Emma Corrin as Elizabeth Bennet.

But those predecessors weren’t in showrunner Dolly Alderton’s mind as she sat down to craft her interpretation of Jane Austen’s most fiercely adored novel. She instead found inspiration in a less traditional Pride and Prejudice. “The one adaptation that I did reference and I found really useful was Bridget Jones,” says Alderton. Not because her version of Lizzy lip-synchs “All by Myself” or accidentally makes blue soup, but because that 2001 film really understands the character of Wickham—the dashing ne’er-do-well Lizzy is drawn toward before she falls for Darcy.

In the novel, says Alderton, “characters were often talking about how charming he was.” But in her estimation, Austen didn’t spend much time actively showing Wickham’s charm or ease of conversation. “The only examples we really saw of his conversation was him complaining about Darcy, being a bit whingey. I was like, I really need to fool the audience into thinking that he’s the guy that Lizzy should be with.”

Corrin and Matthew Duckett as Colonel Fitzwilliam.

The answer lay in Bridget Jones, which reimagines Wickham as the seductive Daniel Cleaver—Bridget’s bad news boss. As Alderton, a novelist herself, explains, “Cleaver lures Bridget in by making her feel like he’s a safe place to land, to gossip about this person that they both hate”—Colin Firth’s standoffish Mark Darcy. “He’s emulated the language of female intimacy to create a false sense of safety in his company. And there was something of Daniel Cleaver’s mischief and playfulness that plays so opposite against what’s perceived as the stiffness of Darcy that I thought was really useful.” So Alderton infused her Wickham with those qualities. Louis Partridge, who plays the role in the new series, feels like a worthy successor to Hugh Grant.

That case study sums up Alderton’s approach to one of the most frequently adapted works in English literature. Her Pride and Prejudice is both artful and thoughtful, a six-episode series that shows deep respect for its source material while teasing out some of the novel’s less obvious threads—with the help of an uncommonly good cast, some of whom can be seen in character for the first time in these exclusive images. The show’s heart and soul may not actually be Corrin’s Elizabeth or Lowden’s Darcy, but instead the marriage-minded Mrs. Bennet, a character whose overwhelming drive to get her five daughters hitched makes her easy to dismiss.

Daryl McCormack as Mr. Bingley, asking Freya Mavor’s Jane to dance.

When one reads Pride and Prejudice as a teen or a 20-something, it’s easy to get swept up in the romance. If you reread it in your mid-30s, though, you may come to the same realization Alderton did: “Mrs. Bennet’s kind of the hero of the whole fucking thing.” Alderton thinks Elizabeth’s mother has never gotten the credit she deserves: “I really felt I’d like justice for Mrs. Bennet,” she says.

Mrs. Bennet needs to help her daughters find husbands not because she’s in cahoots with the patriarchy or because she’s shallowly obsessed with appearances, but because it’s a critical economic imperative. Alderton wrote a poignant scene in which, during the show’s second episode, Mrs. Bennet explains this to her husband. “This is actually really serious, and you shouldn’t be laughing at me,” the showrunner says, paraphrasing the gist of her speech. “You should be recognizing how much I love my children."

It’s a good monologue, made even better by its delivery from Olivia Colman. The Oscar winner was Alderton’s first and only choice for the role. “I wrote an unbelievably emotional love letter to Olivia, begging her to play Mrs. Bennet, because I knew that our Mrs. Bennet couldn’t be played by anyone else,” the showrunner says. No other actor, she says, has Colman’s ability to “ping-pong, in this really effortless and very genuine way, from very high comedy to very real emotional truth. And that’s really the magic of Austen.”

Siena Kelly and Saffron Coomber as Mr. Bingley’s sisters, Caroline Bingley and Louisa Hurst.

Colman has an ideal foil in Rufus Sewell, who plays Mr. Bennet—a character who, on the page, may seem bemused by his wife at best, and contemptuous of her at worst. Alderton, though, chose to portray their union as one that’s essentially happy. “I think a lot of people think it is an antagonistic marriage,” she says. “But for me, they felt like a very recognizable British couple who are extremely comfortable with each other and deeply fond of each other. And how that deep familiarity is expressed is with relentless mockery, its own expression of love.” After all, she adds, the pair did have five children together in very quick succession—“so I’m sure they liked each other a bit.”

Charming as the elder Bennets may be, every iteration of Pride and Prejudice rests upon the actors who play its central couple. As with Colman, Alderton was certain early on that Corrin and Lowden were the two performers for the job. “Emma can balance that very difficult Lizzy combination of emotional depth and vulnerability and wit and sharpness. Emma’s a very, very, very intelligent person, and I think that’s what you need for Lizzy.”

Lowden, meanwhile, seemed up to the task of playing a notoriously tricky part—a man who seems irredeemably cold and snobbish until Elizabeth visits his estate and discovers how differently Darcy acts when he’s comfortable in his surroundings.

“You have to see a lot of complexity, which means that when we see the real him—when we visit him in Pemberley and we see his gentleness and his loyalty and his protectiveness and his kindness—he doesn’t suddenly feel like a stranger,” Alderton says. “You need a really, really robust actor. You need a really, really muscular actor. That’s what Jack is. And of course, he is also all those things that we need Darcy to be: He’s handsome, he’s sexy, he’s masculine, he’s gallant. So it was a no-brainer, really.”

Is there perhaps another handsome, sexy, masculine, iconically British character she’d like to see him play next? Alderton laughs. “I think my answer is ‘no comment.’”

She’s more open about other things, like the research she did while writing the series—with assists from Professor Fiona Stafford, an Oxford literature professor, and another huge name in Austenland: Emma Thompson, who wrote and starred in Ang Lee’s gold standard adaptation of Sense and Sensibility. When they met before the new Pride and Prejudice started shooting, Thompson gave Alderton some key advice: “You cannot underestimate how important the indicators of class and etiquette are within your scenes. They are so much more than just intricacies of a period drama. They’re a language that signifies some of the most important parts of this time of history.”

There’s strong attention to detail in the final product, every episode of which was directed by Euros Lyn, a veteran of British TV. But there’s also a strong vein of humor—which you’d expect to see from Alderton, whose previous work includes the National Book Award–winning memoir Everything I Know About Love and the best-selling comedic novel Good Material—as well as a sensual current.

Lowden’s Mr. Darcy with his sister Georgiana, played by Isabella Sermon.

It’s too soon for Alderton to pinpoint a sexually charged moment from her series that might enter the vernacular, like Darcy’s wet shirt—“I actually had lunch with Andrew Davies a couple of weeks ago, and I was chastising him for writing that scene: ‘It’s never going to get better than that moment with the wet shirt. It kind of ruined it for all future adapters of Pride and Prejudice’”—or Matthew Macfadyen’s famous hand flex. But the mood is there. “What we’ve ended up with is something that I personally find very erotic,” she says lightly—slightly joking, slightly not.

Adapting a property as beloved as Pride and Prejudice might seem like a daunting prospect. To Alderton, however, it felt practically effortless. Austen’s novel can be seamlessly split into six distinct acts; her dialogue is remarkably lively and speakable, even to modern audiences. “I mean, really she did most of the work for me,” says Alderton. “I just wish she was around to have written screenplays, because she was a really cinematic writer.”

The experience has given Alderton a taste for adaptation—and for tackling narratives with settings that go outside her own personal experience. She’d love to try her hand at William Boyd’s Any Human Heart or Iris Murdoch’s The Sea, the Sea. “I’d love to do an epic. I’d love to write something in wartime. I’d love to write something in the Blitz era.

“I just don’t want to be in 2026 anymore,” Alderton says with a laugh. “I basically want to be in any year other than now. That’s where I want to write my next story.”

Halle Berry is known for being something of an open book, as she’s shared aspects of her life and career with her fans over the years. (Of course, she’s also known to share the occasional bikini photo or two.) In more recent years, Berry really hasn’t had a problem publicly highlighting her relationship with boyfriend-turned-fiancé Van Hunt. Comments shared by the Oscar-winning actor and Hunt suggest they have a firm relationship. And, apparently, that’s carried right through her ongoing custody battle.

For weeks now, Berry and ex-husband Olivier Martinez have been engaged in a legal skirmish, with the latter having leveled accusations against the X-Men star. Berry (via her lawyer) has since vehemently denied the claims and has appeared in court a few times. By her side has been Van Hunt, who’s been photographed walking with her after the court hearings she’s attended. According to Page Six, Hunt has been a major source of support for Berry amid the legal proceedings. The outlet’s insider says this:

Van has really been Halle’s rock through all of this. He’s been by her side throughout the whole custody battle and restraining order situation.

Hunt and Berry began dating back in 2020 and, before long the singer/songwriter/music producer began making frequent appearances in Berry’s Instagram posts. Although these latest comments are from an insider, they do appear to align with what’s been said and shown of Berry and Hunt’s romance. The source went on to drop further claims about what Hunt’s presence has meant for his partner throughout this time:

It’s obviously been an incredibly difficult and stressful time for her, but he’s been such a calming presence and a huge source of strength. He’s been incredibly supportive through everything, and having someone like him to lean on has made a big difference for her.

Halle Berry Shared How She And Van Hunt Happened: 'I'm Convinced I Manifested My Now Partner'

As previously alluded to Berry and Hunt have appeared together in more than a few of the former’s social media posts over the last several years. For example, years back, Berry posted about their outing at the NY Spring/Summer 2024 fashion show, and she’s also shared sweet tribute posts to Hunt. Berry is even far past the point at which she’s comfortable sharing her and Hunt’s Christmas festivities.

It was in 2025 that Hunt proposed to Berry, though both of them confirmed around that same time that the Bruised actress had yet to formally accept it. Berry explained that after having been married three times, she wasn’t eager to jump into another marriage right away. In her estimation, she and Hunt also didn’t need to “validate” their love in any way. However, earlier this year, Berry clarified that she did accept the proposal but that she and her partner had yet to set a wedding date.

Halle Berry and Van Hunt have emerged as something of a fan-favorite couple on social media, so many take comfort in the notion of the latter comforting his lady amid these legal proceedings. And, as for when or where the pair might actually tie the knot, that remains to be seen.

#3680. Ratchet & Clank Game Shutting Down Before Ever Fully Launching

Sony Interactive Entertainment and French developer Oh BiBi have announced Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble, a phone and tablet game, is coming to a close before it was even released fully.

In a statement, the developers said the game's final update is coming today, November 6, and the game itself will be removed from digital stores on November 21, 2026.

No information was provided as to why Ranger Rumble is shutting down. The game soft-launched in 2025 in limited territories, and expanded to more markets, but it's no longer going ahead with a full global release.

People who already have the game installed can keep playing until May 1, 2027, which is when the game's servers permanently close. Once the servers are shut down, the game will be completely unplayable.

Ranger Rumble is described as a "fast-paced multiplayer platformer arena shooter" where you battle others on a quest to become a galactic ranger.

In-app purchases have been removed from Ranger Rumble, and if you have a balance of currency, you should spend it before May 1, 2027. Alternatively, you can seek a refund from Apple’s App Store or Google Play.

"On behalf of the dev team and everyone helping to make the game, thanks to our amazing community for all your support, especially to those who have spent time playing, sharing feedback, and helping shape Ranger Rumble throughout its development," the developer said.

The latest entry in the mainline Ratchet & Clank series was 2021's Rift Apart. Its developer, Insomniac Games, has focused on Marvel properties more recently, releasing Marvel's Spider-Man 2 in 2023 and Marvel's Wolverine this year.

#3678. Sam Rockwell Breaks Down Scenes From His Career, Including ‘Charlie’s Angels’ and ‘The White Lotus’

“Thank God for Marvin Gaye and this song,” Sam Rockwell says while watching a younger version of himself dance opposite a stunned Drew Barrymore in the 2000 action-comedy Charlie’s Angels. “I mean, this song really makes the scene.”

While telling stories from his more than 35-year career across film and television for Vanity Fair’s Scene Selection, Rockwell says people tried to stop him from appearing in the remake of the 1970s TV series starring Barrymore, Cameron Diaz, and Lucy Liu. When he joined the project as secretly evil software engineer Eric Knox—who starts the film as Barrymore’s love interest—the script was “a work in progress,” Rockwell recalls. “A lot of people told me not to do this movie. And then, they all ate their words. It had a very specific kind of popcorn vibe to it, very unique, and I don’t think I’ve seen [it] since.”

Rockwell originally envisioned a more “punk rock” direction for his character, but changed his approach after speaking with friend and former Galaxy Quest costar Alan Rickman. “You know, Sam, keep it simple,” Rockwell recalled the late actor telling him. “When I did Die Hard, I killed someone and ate a sandwich.”

Over the decades, Rockwell tried his hand at a mix of projects—somber indies like sci-fi drama Moon (2009), studio awards contenders including The Green Mile (1999), and mainstream fare like Iron Man 2 (2010). “I was dating Leslie Bibb when Iron Man one came out…. It sort of changed superhero movies,” says Rockwell, whose now real-life partner of nearly 20 years appeared in the first film.

After being cast in the sequel as fast-talking arms dealer Justin Hammer, Rockwell learned that he would share most of his scenes with Mickey Rourke as fellow fictional baddie and Russian physicist Ivan Vanko. “Mickey didn’t want to meet me until we were on camera,” Rockwell remembers. “It was a wild experience…. Because my scenes were dialogue-driven, whereas a lot of [the rest of] it was special effects…it was a surprisingly actor-friendly experience being that it was a studio movie for me.”

Bibb and Rockwell, who also shared scenes in Iron Man 2, reunited onscreen in 2025 for season three of The White Lotus as it was filmed in Thailand. He joined the series partway through production, tasked with performing Mike White’s “brilliant monologue” about sex addiction and gender identity opposite Walton Goggins. “Leslie helped me get off-book in South Africa; we were on safari,” says Rockwell, who says he based his searching Buddhist character, Frank, on Martin Sheen in Apocalypse Now.

The actor also detailed the past screen inspiration behind his Oscar-winning performance in Martin McDonagh’s drama, Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri (2017), calling the trajectory of his role as a bigoted local cop, “[The Andy Griffith Show’s] Barney Fife becomes [Taxi Driver’s] Travis Bickle,” says Rockwell. He joins forces with McDonagh once more for the new awards-season contender Wild Horse Nine, in which he acts with teenage idol John Malkovich. “I love characters who change and are underestimated by the audience,” says Rockwell of Three Billboards. “And this is really that.”

#3677. GTA+: Price, Free Games, And All The Other Perks You Get With A Membership Ahead Of GTA 6 Launch

In 2022, Rockstar Games introduced GTA+, a subscription service that provides a variety of perks and bonuses in GTA Online--and beyond.

With GTA 6's release coming up this month, we're running through everything you need to know about GTA +. Do you really need to sign up for yet another subscription service? Only you can answer that, but below you'll find a breakdown of the key facts about GTA+ to help you decide.

In This Article
  • What Is GTA+?
  • Free Games And Other Perks
  • How Much Is GTA+?
  • How To Sign Up For GTA+
  • GTA 6?
  • Take-Two "Thrilled" With GTA+

What Is GTA+?

GTA+ is a subscription service for GTA Online that originally debuted in March 2022 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The subscription offering came to PC for the first time with GTA 5 Enhanced's launch in March 2025.

Free Games And Other Perks

To begin with, every GTA+ subscriber gets 500,000 worth of GTA$ deposited automatically into their in-game accounts monthly based on their billing date. Members also get a 15% bonus in GTA$ for Shark Card purchases, while they also earn GTA$ multipliers for certain GTA Online missions and modes. Subscribers also get discounts on in-game items, with discounted wares varying month by month.

GTA+ members also get access to The Vinewood Car Club where they can claim free vehicles. Also in terms of vehicles, subscribers get a 100-car garage, spread across five floors.

Members receive monthly benefits--for November 2026, Rockstar is offering the Grotti Itali RSX sports car for free, along with the new Chameleon Paints, and more items for your mansion.

You can visit this page to see the current month's special bonuses for subscribers.

Another major perk of signing up for GTA+ is getting access to the GTA+ Games Library. This is a rotating selection of classic Rockstar titles that players have access to for as long as their membership remains active. The current roster of freebies--as of November 2026--includes a range of titles for PC, console, and mobile:

  • GTA 5
  • Red Dead Redemption
  • GTA Online
  • GTA Vice City - The Definitive Edition
  • GTA III - The Definitive Edition
  • Bully
  • GTA: The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition
  • LA Noire
  • GTA: Liberty City Stories
  • GTA: Chinatown Wars

How Much Is GTA+?

GTA+ launched in 2022 priced at $6/month, but the price went up to $8/month in 2024. Memberships can be canceled at any time. There is no multi-month or annual subscription option.

How To Sign Up For GTA+

GTA+ requires a copy of GTA V or GTA Online. You can sign up on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S through those platforms' store pages or from within GTA Online. On PC, people can sign up via their preferred store or in game.

GTA 6?

Rockstar Games has not said anything yet about if GTA+ will be supported with GTA 6. Given that GTA 5's GTA Online may stick around even after GTA 6 launches, it's possible GTA+ will continue to be supported for that game at least. It's expected that GTA 6 will have a significant online mode given the huge success of GTA Online, but it remains to be seen what form it may take.

While we don't know if GTA+ will give you anything extra or new in GTA 6, Rockstar has confirmed that all preorders of GTA 6 come with a free month of GTA+. It auto-renews, so be sure to cancel if you don't want to keep it.

Take-Two "Thrilled" With GTA+

In 2022, Rockstar owner Take-Two commented on GTA+'s introduction, saying the company was "thrilled" with the response out of the gate.

"We're thrilled about how it's been rolled out so far. We're thrilled with the conversion rate," Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick said back then. "And it's clear, that consumers really like the opportunity to engage with GTA Online and they value... what we're offering through a subscription."

Take-Two hasn't said a whole lot about GTA+ in the ensuing years, but the company loves the kind of recurring revenue that a subscription service provides.

#3676. Where Is Joran van der Sloot Now? Inside His Life in Prison

Nearly two decades after Natalee Holloway disappeared while on a high school graduation trip to Aruba, Joran van der Sloot admitted to killing the teen after they were spotted leaving a club together on the night she went missing.

Following the release of Netflix’s November 2026 docuseries Taken: Natalee Holloway, viewers may be wondering where van der Sloot is today after he admitted to killing Holloway and Stephany Flores Ramírez.

Everything to know about van der Sloot’s crimes and life today, below.

Van der Sloot is currently in custody at Challapalca prison in Peru after he was sentenced to 28-year prison sentence for the 2010 murder of Ramírez, which is concurrently running alongside his 20-year federal prison sentence in the United States for extortion and wire fraud.

Van der Sloot married his ex-wife, Leidy Figueroa, in July 2014 at the prison where he is still serving his sentence. His attorney confirmed to CNN that Figueroa was an accountant and had one child at the time she married van der Sloot.

The former couple welcomed their daughter on September 30, 2014, which was just three months after they tied the knot.

His attorney confirmed to the Daily Mail in 2023 that van der Sloot was divorcing Figueroa and was moving on.

“Joran had a bunch of girlfriends,” his lawyer said at the time. “Lots of girls used to visit him.”

Holloway vanished on May 30, 2005, while celebrating her high school graduation in Oranjestad, Aruba. She was last seen leaving the Carlos’n Charlie’s nightclub and getting into a car with van der Sloot and brothers Deepak Kalpoe and Satish Kalpoe.

Van der Sloot was quickly named a suspect in the case after the accounts he gave to authorities didn’t line up. Alongside the Kalpoe brothers, van der Sloot was arrested in June 2005 on suspicion of kidnapping and murder. However, all three men were released without charges that September. The group was arrested for a second time in November 2007 and they were released again one month later.

Aruban officials reopened the case against van der Sloot in 2008 after Dutch crime reporter Peter R. de Vries released hidden-camera footage that showed him describing Holloway’s death. However, the case fell apart when officials couldn’t corroborate the statements he made in the footage.

Five years after Holloway’s disappearance, van der Sloot killed 21-year-old college student Ramírez in Lima, Peru. He fled to Chile, but was ultimately arrested in June 2010 for her murder.

That same month, van der Sloot was also indicted in the United States on federal wire fraud and extortion charges tied to a March 2010 meeting he had with Natalee’s mother, Beth Holloway. During the meeting, he demanded that Beth pay him money in exchange for information about Natalee’s disappearance.

Van der Sloot pleaded guilty to the federal extortion charges in 2023 and was sentenced to 20 years. As part of the plea deal, he finally admitted to killing Natalee and agreed to share information about her death.

Aruba enforces a 12-year statute of limitations for homicides, meaning that the time limit to convict him has expired.

In Netflix’s Taken: Natalee Holloway, Beth explained that she’s spent the past two years working with Netherlands attorneys Royce de Vries and Annemiek van Spanje to file a murder complaint against van der Sloot with Dutch authorities.

“I’ve been working busy behind the scenes, got the murder complaint,” she said. “And now we’re working on, hopefully, murder charges. So I’ve been busy, but one step at a time.”

She added that it is her “new mission” to get justice for Natalee.

This weekend, Saturday Night Live welcomed comedian Druski as its latest host for Season 52, and some serious history was made. On the one hand, there was the fact that Druski became the first social media-birthed star to host SNL. And, on the other hand, I’m not sure I’ve ever seen the long-running sketch comedy series have such an eclectic assortment of stars. Chris Rock was just one of the notable names to show up to root on the Internet celebrity, and I’m shook by this roster of talent.

During Druski’s opening monologue, he was joined by Emma Stone, his co-star in the upcoming comedy film The Catch. The Oscar winner’s appearance was surprising enough on its own and, before that, the new senator-elect of Texas, James Talarico, appeared in the opening monologue alongside James Austin Johnson’s President Trump. The notion of Rock, Stone and Talarico being on the same episode of SNL is wild, but check out the clip from X down below to see all the other big names who appeared during the goodbyes:

Wow, I don't know what the hell is even happening, Dave Chappelle and Chris Rock showed up, with Walton Goggins, Michael B. Jordan and even Austin Butler (left side, blue cap) were there hanging out with Druski! https://t.co/8pRxYQTdTuNovember 8, 2026

I honestly can’t remember the last time I’ve seen such a mix of stars during a single episode of Saturday Night Live, and that’s saying a lot, given the show’s history. Over the years, SNL has treated viewers to some truly jaw-dropping celebrity cameos. And while there’s much to be said for the graphical improvements of Ocarina 4K Electric Boogaloo over BotW, what’s more fascinating is how the similarities reinforce the idea that the worlds of OoT and BotW, separated by different game mechanics and stories and thousands of in-world years, are nevertheless the same.

And all that’s left of Lon Lon Ranch by the time Breath of the Wild occurs are a few long-abandoned remnants of the place that Malon and Talon once called home.

#3673. Mass Effect Is Getting A New Art Collection At A Difficult Time For Its Fans

The Mass Effect Collection

Moor-Art says it began collaborating with BioWare over a year ago to release a new selection of limited-edition posters. "What began as a celebration of an ongoing saga now feels like the bastion in the continuation of a studio's legacy," the studio said in a press release.

The collection from Moor-Art is inspired by the characters and worlds of Mass Effect, with the original artwork being produced by acclaimed artists and Mass Effect die-hard fans Matt Essom and Dan Mumford. The designs will also be available as T-shirts. The first one is by Essom, and Moor-Art says this illustration captures the spirit and emotional depth of the series, as well as the bonds forged on the Normandy as her crew traveled to unknown worlds. This will be limited to 200 hand-numbered prints worldwide, plus 30 Giclée prints with a certificate of authenticity signed by the artist.

Mumford's "Mass Effect 2" poster aims to capture the sci-fi horror elements of the confrontations against the Reapers, and it features a full ensemble of crew members. Only 150 hand-numbered prints for each variant will be produced, alongside 30 Giclée prints of each Shepard variant, with a certificate of authenticity signed by the artist. #3672. The Curious Case of Olivia Reingold’s AI Photo at a Democratic Victory Party: Valentino, Chanel, and a Free Press Mystery

On Monday night, the eve of the 2026 midterm elections, the fashion crowd celebrated at the 2026 CFDA Fashion Awards, colloquially referred to as the Oscars of American fashion. Tory Burch was honored with the Positive Change Award, which was presented to her by Anna Wintour, the global editorial director of Vogue and chief content officer of Condé Nast. In her remarks, Wintour made the evening’s only direct reference to the midterms, reminiscing about attending a fundraising event for James Talarico, who successfully flipped Texas in the race for the Senate last night, alongside Burch. After applause from the audience, Wintour, a prolific Democratic fundraiser herself, looked up and addressed the room: “Let’s hope all of Texas feels the way you do,” she said.

The American fashion crowd has largely distanced itself from politics since the 2024 election. During their time in the White House as first ladies, Michelle Obama and Jill Biden were staunch supporters of the American fashion industry, often wearing American designers for public appearances. Melania Trump, in contrast, has more often preferred European labels. It’s an MO that trickles down into the political parties they represent.

There were many headlines that came out of last night’s midterms: Talarico flipped Texas, Annie Andrews flipped South Carolina, New Hampshire’s Chris Pappas became the first out gay man to be elected to the Senate, and Keisha Lance Bottoms of Georgia and Deb Haaland of New Mexico became the first Black and Native American women, respectively, to be elected governor in the history of the US.

And yet it wasn’t just good news (and many great memes) that circulated in my group chats last night; there were also some fashion choices worth noting. First, the most pressing: Where were Steve Kornacki’s khakis? And what was the reasoning behind Haley Stevens’s ludicrously capacious hat? Some questions in life simply go unanswered.

Kornacki, a national political correspondent for NBC News, does not make his political affiliations public. But men in his age range (he is 47) and in the generations that follow—millennials and Gen Z—have been contending with what formalwear means and signals today.

Democratic men have been hard at work on their public image since the 2024 election, largely distancing themselves from the MAGA look and its too-large suits and extra-wide ties. In separating themselves from the manosphere, men like Abdul El-Sayed, who won the Senate race in Michigan, and Jon Ossoff, who was reelected to the Senate in Georgia, have been dressing more like the less buttoned up, progressive men they represent and less like the old establishment politicians on both the right and the left.

On the campaign trail, El-Sayed often sported tees and sweaters rather than button-downs and ties, frequently wearing taut sweaters and henleys under his suit jacket, while Ossoff largely opted for rolled cuffs and no jacket. As the two delivered victory speeches last night, they each wore a tailored suit—a little too tight in the arms; these are men who seem to eat their fair share of protein—and ditched their tie.

It’s a familiar image of a more laid-back look, but one in stark contrast to that of the faces of the right: Donald Trump, JD Vance, et al. Ossoff and El-Sayed, similarly to Kamala Harris during her presidential bid, also leaned into what was happening on the internet. These days, netizens are happy to objectify men and christen a new internet boyfriend every week. Ossoff’s and El-Sayed’s campaigns seemed to understand the power of thirst—that their suits were too tight was most likely not completely intentional, but it did help underscore a simple fact: that they are fit, and that their virility can be both attractive and nonthreatening all at once.

Zohran Mamdani speaking at an event on election night. Mamdani also ditched his tie on Tuesday, in line with some of his fellow Democrats.

It is worth noting, however, that there are some men further to the left, both in politics and around it, who have reembraced the suit: Zohran Mamdani and Hasan Piker. On one hand, this has served a similar purpose as Ossoff’s and El-Sayed’s choices: It has distanced them from looksmaxxers and other conservative-leaning young men. On the other hand, a suit for Mamdani and Piker signifies what suits have always represented: that these are grown men doing important things.

The men are not the full story, however. Bottoms and Haaland came as they are, nodding to the communities they represent. The former wore a bright fuchsia suit and matching blouse, a callback to the lively and monochromatic dressing that is a deeply embedded and celebrated tradition in Black church culture. Haaland’s jewelry—firefly earrings and a beaded necklace—nodded at the style of accessories that is representative of Native style and fashion. If there is something that fashion clearly signifies, it’s community and belonging.

It is a running punch line that the left is more closely connected to fashion—it’s the wine-and-cheese crowd, the elites. (Hillary Clinton, during her bid for the presidency in 2016, was dragged online and by the press for wearing an Armani jacket that reportedly retailed for some $12,000 while delivering a speech that touched on income inequality.) While it’s true that fashion designers are often more enthusiastic about dressing progressives than they are about dressing conservatives, in the era of Trump and the MAGA look, this has become a half-baked story.

Olivia Reingold, a staff writer at The Free Press, made a post on X last night while reporting from an event for the Michigan Democratic Party. “So far at Abdul El-Sayed’s election night event I’ve spotted, Valentino heels, a Chanel bag, a Moncler jacket, Rolex watches, and a YSL bag among other designer items,” Reingold wrote, captioning an image of a woman holding a gold quilted Chanel handbag and a pair of Valentino Rockstud leather pumps.

Read Fit Check: Your front row seat to the power players, peacocks, and deep pockets of fashion—and how they influence the rest of the world.

When one takes a closer look, however, the image has several discrepancies. The style and make of the Chanel Flap bag is inconsistent with others the brand has sold, and the Valentino shoes in question appear askew in proportion; their straps have several punched holes that the authentic Valentino style does not. This could mean that the products in the image are not authentic, but there is another suggestive tell: The bottom strap on the left shoe appears to cut through its connecting strap rather than around, a classic mistake made when artificial intelligence is used to create or alter an image. A run of the image through several AI detectors, including SynthID, a digital watermarking approach created by Google DeepMind that detects media generated by OpenAI, Google, Nvidia, and Kakao, suggests the use of AI. SynthID detected that “this media was made or edited with OpenAI.” (Vanity Fair has reached out to Chanel and Valentino to advise on the authenticity of the products.)

Reingold did not reply to a request for comment, but on Thursday afternoon followed up with a new post on X, admitting to using AI “to brighten and sharpen an image of a woman in Valentino shoes and a Chanel bag.”

It’s become too easy to try to make a point about the left’s fashion choices: that Rama Duwaji, wife of Mamdani, should not wear pricey shoes, even if borrowed, because of her political beliefs; or that Democratic women should not carry Valentino or Chanel and vote for a candidate seeking to tax the wealthy. Therein lies the crux of the argument: Does this mean that luxury shoppers should align themselves with MAGA because it’s a party associated with billionaires like Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos and logo-clad celebs like Nicki Minaj, who wore Chanel to the polls in New Hampshire? The answer is simple: no.

Our fashion choices say much about our values, identity, and aspirations. And while politicians have oftentimes utilized fashion to align themselves with specific groups or appear friendly to voters, they, in broad strokes, do not define our political affiliations. A Chanel bag does not make a Democrat, just as a red tie does not make a Republican.

#3671. You Can Finally Drive A Dreamcast, Thanks To Sonic

Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds is gearing up for a second year of action, and while you can expect new courses, modes, and characters to join the game, the real headline act here is the new cars coming to it. As part of the Sega Consoles Pack, players will be able to tear around courses while driving a four-wheeled Sega video game console, with each vehicle expertly blending the design of that classic gaming hardware into a lean-and-mean racing machine.

The new cars are based on the Sega Genesis (or Mega Drive for anyone who lived outside the US), the Sega Saturn, and Sega's final home console, the Dreamcast. According to the Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds development team, the idea was to incorporate design elements that would instantly remind players of each console into their respective vehicle frames, like the rounded form of the Dreamcast or the angular silhouettes and subdued tones of the Saturn. The team even went so far as to recreate the Dreamcast’s Visual Memory Unit using original reference data from that era.

"Rather than directly recreating the hardware itself, we translated rounded forms into fenders and nose sections, while angular lines became body panels and hoods, adding the sense of speed expected from a racing machine," the development team explained in a PlayStation Blog post. "While preserving recognizable colors and components from each system, we also designed around the game’s front-and-rear combination mechanic, incorporating the fun of pairing consoles and controllers into the vehicles themselves."

The end result is a design that instantly clues you in on which console informed its design, while still looking like it can burn some rubber on the track. Sega said that the "Genesis Tower" proved to be challenging and required considerable experimentation so that it wouldn't interfere with various visual elements, but it managed to nail the design in the end.

In addition to the Sega Console cars, Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds will also get a new Duel Mode that is designed to offer a different experience from the standard 12-player races. Each race is a one-on-one showdown, and it will require players to think strategically as they jockey for pole position against their rival.

Released in 2025, Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds has steadily grown with more content throughout its first year. Alongside Sonic and the rest of the Mobius crew, the game has also seen some interesting crossovers announced, like a team-up with the nihilistic mecha anime series Neon Genesis Evangelion. If you're interested in checking it out, you can grab the game on PC for $22 at Fanatical currently.

Video game adaptations have a way of making everybody angry. However, I can understand why Zach Cregger expected a different conversation around his Resident Evil movie. The director behind Barbarian and Weapons has opened up about the one part of releasing his 2026 movie calendar horror hit that genuinely "frustrated" him, and I get where he's coming from.

During an appearance on The Town with Matthew Belloni, Cregger was asked whether he'd consider tackling another established franchise after Resident Evil. His answer led to a candid discussion about the reaction to his film, which follows Austin Abrams' medical courier Bryan through a nightmare in Raccoon City. Cregger felt people cared more about what he changed from Capcom's games than about the movie itself. He explained:

I think I was frustrated at the conversation around Resident Evil and how much of the conversation really didn't have anything to do with the movie. It had everything to do with whether the movie was living up to the different standards that different fans of the games had, whether it was using the characters or not, or what did I get wrong in the lore, or why is it? It was just a lot about why isn't this like the source material or why is it good that it's not like the [source material].

I can understand why that would be exhausting. After spending years making a new horror movie, you release it into the world, and suddenly everyone argues about why Leon Kennedy isn't included. However, I also empathize with fans who have waited a long time to see their favorite characters properly adapted.

Cregger chose to tell an original story within the Resident Evil universe instead of recreating one of the games, and the movie's biggest strength has nothing to do with lore or Easter eggs. His movie swaps familiar protagonists for Bryan and leans into the sensation of playing survival horror: limited resources, increasingly awful encounters and the knowledge that the next room might be your last. Before release, some fans objected to the missing characters and changes to Raccoon City.

What's interesting is that the movie did incredibly well. Resident Evil has earned more than $400 million worldwide, according to Box Office Mojo, while Rotten Tomatoes lists a 96% critics' score. Early reviews praised RE for its relentless pacing and the way Cregger captured the experience of playing the games.

Still, success didn't erase Cregger's disappointment with the discussion surrounding it. He continued:

All the conversation just felt like it was about not the movie. And I'm proud of the movie. I really love the movie. I should have known better going into it. I should have understood that that was going to be the case, but for some reason I was a little shocked.

That last admission is what stuck with me. Cregger is a fan himself, and he previously acknowledged that players hoping for Leon's story had a fair reason to feel disappointed. But he also wanted people to judge the actual movie he made. Surely there's room for both opinions.

Zach Cregger's not necessarily finished with Raccoon City, either. He told Belloni he'd like some creative input if the series continues, even if somebody else directs the next installment. Personally, I hope he gets that chance. Given how well this one turned out, I'd much rather see what else he dreams up than spend another round arguing about which character didn't show up.

Resident Evil arrived on digital video-on-demand (VOD) platforms to rent or buy on November 3, 2026, so check your favorite streamer for details.

#3667. Russell Brand Has Been Found Guilty. American Courts Could Learn a Lot From His Trial

Britain’s most notorious serial killers and infamous gangsters are convicted at London’s Old Bailey, under a neo-Baroque dome and gold-gilded statue of Lady Justice. But it is Southwark Crown Court, an entirely bland heap of 1980s bricks by the River Thames, where the embattled entertainers wash up.

Only recently, this is where rapper Chris Brown—who pleaded guilty to affray after striking a man in the head with a glass bottle in a nightclub—learned he would avoid prison. It is also where Russell Brand today was found guilty of one count of rape and three of sexual assault. He was found not guilty of two other counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault.

The week before, whilst reporting on Brand’s trial, I watched a fan in the corridor outside the courtroom admiringly accost the comedian. “I’ve been told to tell you there are many who support you,” she told him. He gave a zen reply: “I receive it, I receive it.” But by and large, English courts are not interested in fame.

In England, the court is an uncontaminated information space: There are no cameras to broadcast what happens inside, and there are strict rules to marshal what information can come in. It may be one of the few places on earth where an influencer can no longer influence; even Katy Perry, Brand’s ex-wife, had to be explained to the judge. In 2026, the closest the US has come to creating a similar environment is Taylor Swift’s wedding.

In a world of video clips, this courtroom is unclippable. What happens here is beyond the reach of rubbernecking pundits or home sleuths wanting a hot take for their socials. Unlike in modern discourse, there are rules in this court, and they are strictly enforced: Complainants in sexual cases are entitled to immediate and lifelong anonymity in the UK. Their real names and identifying details were heard in court—but mention them outside, and you risk arrest for contempt of court. Here, the defense also must ask the judge’s permission to bring up the accusers’ sexual history. When it was suspected that one blogger may have crossed the line, the judge barked at the lead prosecutor: “You’ve plenty of police officers back there…. Send one to arrest him!” They promptly did, and he was ultimately released with a caution.

Jurors, too, can never be unmasked, and their deliberations are forever secret. I sat watching them throughout the trial, but can never tell you what I observed.

From the initial charging to the conclusion of the trial, we in the British media are limited to reporting fairly and accurately only what the jury hears each day. Anyone weighing in publicly with an opinion, a prediction, or anything that could create a “substantial risk of serious prejudice or impediment” to the trial risks joining Brand in the dock of a criminal court. This meant there was no spin as Brand stepped down from the witness stand—no online reprisals against his accusers.

In court, Brand described himself as someone who had once been “staggeringly” famous. His defense argued that, in 2023, reporting from Channel 4, The Times, and The Sunday Times alleging sexual misbehavior changed that—and made everyone desert him. This, Brand said, is why only three witnesses were called to support him—two, if you exclude his wife.

“It’s not the case you’ve been completely abandoned,” wily prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones stated in cross-examination on October 28. Eight seconds of silent staring was Brand’s reply.

“You have a platform with followers in the millions, don’t you?” Silence.

“Yes,” he eventually returned, albeit quietly. Even Harold Pinter would have shouted, “Get on with it.”

Keeping up? To follow any of this is to wade through a thicket of non-sequitur arguments, florid vocabulary and, in his latest twist, the Gospels.

How has Brand’s flimflam, wrapped up in the needy personality of an entertainer who lives off clicks, landed in England’s criminal court system? Uncomfortably, I would say. Southwark is dilapidated and definitely analogue. The litigators wore robes and horsehair wigs, and the microphone on the prosecutor’s lectern was held in place with an enormous amount of yellow and black hazard duct tape. The lights went out twice because of a power cut.

If the world is now video-first, our courts are video-last. With the occasional exception of a judge’s sentencing remarks, nothing in court is photographed, filmed, or recorded for the media. Even the court artist can only take written notes, and must do their actual sketches outside.

“It’s not theater,” I heard the court clerk tell a law student who’d come to watch Brand’s trial but was annoyed to find the six public seats were full.

If this case had been undertaken in Brand’s adopted home of Florida, everyone’s evidence would have been tailored to win over cable news panel pundits. Soundbites would trump reasoned long-form arguments. The names of his accusers would likely be public—as would anything else anyone could dig up about them. Did the framers of the American Constitution really want @truecrimesleuthboy unpicking old Facebook albums of women alleging rape, or network news cameras hounding jurors on their decision?

Did you watch the Amber Heard–versus–Johnny Depp defamation trial in 2022? Were you one of the billions using #AmberTurd online as the “courtroom porn,” as Monica Lewinsky called it for Vanity Fair, was dissected, criticized, and memed? After her defeat, Heard’s lawyer spoke out in frustration: “There’s no way [the jury] couldn’t have been influenced” by the online discussion, she said. “It was horrible.”

Because of where Brand’s trial took place, his testimony could never have been turned into a similar show. In Court 3, there was no camera awaiting his reactions to what he was allegedly being subjected to. Maybe that’s why he didn’t try to pull any of that.

Brand did arrive at court with a Holy Bible bursting with index tabs. One day, when stuck in the corridor with the assembled press pack, he also uncomfortably boomed out, “This is a great day.” But for the most part, I observed him sitting tall and still and lonely in the dock. His personal bodyguard dozed in the courtroom’s family and friends section as an assistant scrolled through her phone and his father demolished a Snickers.

The only sign his group was listening to the awful things their friend/boss/son was being accused of was the very active facial expressions of Brand’s wife, Laura. “Oh, come on,” she appeared to mouth on one occasion, listening to one woman alleging rape.

There was no sign of Brand the comedian or Brand the YouTuber when the defendant took to the witness stand—though he did begin his testimony defiantly, answering the first question with a “No” so loud he seemed to shock even himself. From then on, he diminuendoed so far that the judge jumped in: “You are starting to drop your voice.”

Brand’s silences began when prosecution advocate Karmy-Jones took to her feet. A distinguished prosecutor and defender, she’s worked with and around murderers, sex offenders, and organized crooks. She’s also done time with terrible showoffs, having begun her career as a theater director. Kristin Scott Thomas or a young Lauren Bacall might play her in the film version of the trial.

Karmy-Jones was achingly polite as she unpicked what Brand called his “escalating recollection” of events. In four police interviews across 18 months, claimed Brand, he had no memory of the six women accusing him—even when given photographs, names, and some details. The British version of the Miranda warning tells suspects under caution, “You do not have to say anything. But it may harm your defense if you do not mention when questioned something which you later rely on in court.”

According to the police tapes, so-called Woman 3 did not ring a bell for him back then. But in the witness box, Brand described meeting her at a bar, recalling that a friend had said something like, “There’s a bird here who really wants to meet you.” He remembered that she had “prominent eyes,” was “lithe, elfic, pixyish,” and consented to go to the toilet for “kissing..fondling.” He was found guilty of sexually assaulting her, and acquitted on that charge of rape.

“Are you sure you aren’t piecing an account together from the evidence that was served?” Karmy-Jones asked.

Maybe the lack of spotlight and vodcaster microphone lowered his guard. This proud wordsmith did not seem ready for his words to be used against him. He wouldn’t have sexually assaulted a woman he was flirting with, Brand said. He would have been “complimentary, flirtatious, tactile.” Yet when Brand tried to drift into generalities, he was dragged back to specifics.

“Not if you met someone, Mr Brand. What was the conversation you had?” What did he mean when he said he would have been “tactile?” “Tactile means touch,” was his gently smug reply.

“Indeed it does,” Karmy-Jones returned, dragging him back to the allegation that he had grabbed the woman’s breasts.

When was the last time Brand had been spoken to like this? He did not seem to enjoy it. He even conceded there were “small details” in his evidence “that are inconsistent, and I acknowledge that.”

Perhaps you can see why Brand and his advocates didn’t attempt any “this is a deep state conspiracy sparked by my client’s vlogging about Pfizer” material on the witness stand. During the trial, he somehow managed to maneuver himself into a difficult position: insisting that despite not remembering it previously, he did have a conversation with Woman 5 about consent in which she agreed to unprotected anal sex, even though she’d just insisted their consensual vaginal sex involve a condom. “Nonsense, wasn’t it, Mr. Brand?” asked Karmy-Jones. The jury must have agreed. Brand was found guilty of this charge.

The jury was given the space to examine all this without any public discourse crowding their own thoughts out of their head. And it’s clear to the rest of us that this is preferable: A Gallup poll this year suggested just 17% of Americans have confidence in their criminal justice system. Compare that to the latest Crime Survey for England and Wales, which found 48% have confidence in how criminal justice is administered.

Our courts need physical repair, better pay, more money generally. But the fundamentals are right and working.

On one of the last days of the Brand trial, I left the court building and recognized one of the jurors standing in front of me. They had their coat on, a bag on their shoulder, and were stepping out into a cold London evening totally anonymously. A thick gaggle of paparazzi, waiting for Russell and co., were lined up at the boundary. The juror slipped through without a single flashbulb going off, without a single paparazzo glancing or realizing this person might be someone worth photographing. That is exactly how it should be.

#3666. Can You Upgrade To GTA 6’s $100 Edition? Yes, And It’s Easy–Here’s How

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19. If you're planning to buy the $80 edition but want to upgrade later to the $100 version, you might be interested to know if such a thing is possible.

Thankfully, yes, it is-and it's very easy to do.

Rockstar will offer an "Ultimate Edition Upgrade" for $20, so for anyone who buys the $80 version and decides they do want the additional perks, they can upgrade. This applies to both the digital edition of GTA 6 that you can buy from the Xbox and PlayStation stores, as well the code-in-a-box physical edition.

The $100 Ultimate Edition, which is not sold in stores, includes a lot of extras, including vehicles, weapons, clothing for your in-game characters. The items are "threaded across all aspects of Jason and Lucia's story," Rockstar said, with new items becoming available "behind each chapter." Additionally, people who buy the $100 version get access to in-game businesses that won't be available to everyone else, including a hair salon, a tattoo parlor, a mod shop, and more.

Meanwhile, all preorders for GTA 6 come with the The Vintage Vice City Pack
and one month of GTA+.

In other news, preloading for GTA 6 begins November 10, and that's good news considering the game weighs in at a whopping 212GB. The game officially unlocks at midnight local time, so pack your bags for New Zealand if you want to play it sooner.

It’s no secret that Heated Rivalry is one of the biggest book-to-screen adaptations of recent years. The smutty, queer hockey romance stole the hearts of fans everywhere when it was released in late 2025, and its popularity hasn’t wavered at all. Fans are only going to get more intense now that news has dropped that Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie will be suiting up for a third season as well. However, I'm concerned about one detail.

Fans of Heated Rivalry have already known about Season 2 kicking off production, as photos from the set have been leaked despite the show’s creator, Jacob Tierney, kindly asking fans to give them space while filming. The news about a third season has been highly speculated, and now, that has been confirmed as well. Both seasons are reportedly being filmed back-to-back. This theoretically means that there shouldn’t be a huge wait between seasons, and maybe fans could get all twelve episodes sometime next year.

In addition to two more seasons with Shane and Ilya, Deadline reports that Tierney is working on a standalone theatrical release that the trade believes will be a “Christmas special” or “holiday-themed episode” centered around Season 1, Episode 3 couple Scott (François Arnaud) and Kip (Robbie G.K.). It’s not the Heated Rivalry-centric bonus episode fans have been hoping for, but the holiday special could be inspired by the short holiday story author Rachel Reid penned for the couple and earlier this year took down from her official website.

As a fan of the sports drama series, I’m overjoyed at the news, but I do have one concern heading into these news seasons when it comes to what it might mean for Shane and Ilya’s relationship.

Unlike the other couples in Reid’s Game Changers book universe, Shane and Ilya’s relationship unfolds over several books. When the series was released (and subsequently renewed for a second and a secret third season), the couple’s second book, The Long Game, was the final installment in their relationship. But then Reid announced she was writing a third book, Unrivaled, centered on the fan-favorite couple.

Had Reid not made the announcement that she was writing Unrivaled, I would have confidently said that Tierney and the creative team behind Heated Rivalry planned to split The Long Game into two seasons. This would allow the show to really dig deep into Shane and Ilya’s relationship challenges and give fans a faithful adaptation like the first season did. It would also provide space for the show to explore some of the other couples in the Game Changes universe, which seems to be happening based on casting announcements for Season 2.

Splitting The Long Game into two seasons might still be the case, which is great news for fans of the novel; however, it does raise concerns about the potential for an adaptation of Unrivaled. After all, if Seasons 2 and 3 are centered on the second novel, then the show would need to be renewed for a fourth season in order to see the third book and the presumed conclusion of Shane and Ilya’s love story on screen.

Given the show’s popularity, a hypothetical fourth season seems like a no-brainer, but one also has to consider the schedules of the cast and crew. With Storrie and Williams both cast in new shows and movies, it might be hard to get them on board for another season beyond these next two. Still, I’d like to believe that the talented actors would be eager to see Ilya and Shane's storyline through to the end.

All of this is purely speculation, as we don't know much about Season 2 of Heated Rivalry other than it's expected to drop in Spring 2027. When that happens, we'll know what to expect from Season 3. Until then, I’ll be streaming, or as fans have dubbed it “reheating,” Season 1 of Heated Rivalry with my HBO Max subscription. Fans can also catch the episodes playing for a limited time in theaters in the US and Canada.

#3664. Mom Sentenced After Abandoning Her 2 Young Children During Hurricane

A Louisiana woman was sentenced to life in prison more than two years after prosecutors said she abandoned her two young sons outside during hurricane conditions, causing her 4-year-old to drown near a highway.

Aaliyah N. Jack, of Lake Charles, was handed a life sentence on Thursday, November 5, in connection with her 4-year-old son’s death, according to a news release from the Calcasieu Parish District Attorney’s Office.

She also received a 15-year sentence in connection with the abandonment of her younger son, who was only 1 year old.

Jack, now 28, abandoned her 4-year-old son, Legend, at a welcome center off of Interstate 10 in southwestern Louisiana before he was found dead in a nearby body of water in July 2024, according to prosecutors.

Afterward, she allegedly left her son, Kingtrail, in a ditch on the side of the highway, where he survived for two days until a truck driver discovered the boy by himself.

Legend was found behind a welcome center in Vinton, near the Texas border, during stormy conditions stemming from a hurricane on July 8, 2024, per NBC affiliate KPLC-TV. (An autopsy confirmed Legend had drowned.)

That day, Hurricane Beryl made landfall in Texas, according to the National Weather Service.

Kingtrail was reportedly found crawling toward the highway the next morning, not far from where Legend died.

Calcasieu Parish Sheriff Stitch Guillory described the 1-year-old as a “miracle baby” at time, according to KPLC-TV. Guillory said the boy was found with insect bites after he was abandoned.

Before her sentencing, Jack was found guilty on September 14 of second-degree murder and cruelty to juveniles, according to the Calcasieu Parish District Attorney’s Office.

According to The Advocate, prosecutors alleged during the trial that Jack had been unhappy with a custody agreement involving her children and Legend’s paternal grandmother, Dion Polk, before she put the boys in her car and abandoned them while driving to Houston.

Polk told the outlet she felt relief following Jack’s conviction. She also said Legend loved his little brother.

“I felt like justice was served for Legend because that’s what it was about,” Polk said. “It was about Legend and Kingtrail.”

In a statement on Thursday, Calcasieu Parish District Attorney Stephen Dwight said Jack’s sentence ensures she “will spend the rest of her life behind bars, held accountable for the horrific actions that took the life of an innocent child and caused unimaginable suffering to another.”

“A life sentence for murder, followed by an additional 15 years for cruelty to juveniles, reflects the severity of these crimes and the lasting harm inflicted on these children,” Dwight added. “While no sentence can undo what happened or restore the life that was lost, we hope this outcome brings some measure of justice and closure.”

#3663. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Under Investigation Following Affair With Suspected Chinese Spy

Nvidia has announced that it has opened an official investigation into its CEO, Jensen Huang, after he admitted that he was involved in an affair with a business executive who is suspected of being a Chinese spy.

Following a New York Times report about Huang's affair with Megaspeed executive and Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang / Huang Le, the Nvidia CEO addressed the situation in a company letter (via the BBC). "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," Huang wrote. "Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, Nvidia's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully."

US intelligence believes that Huang was unaware of Alice Huang's alleged activities, and the security branch reportedly has surveillance of her feeding intel to Beijing. The Nvidia board says Huang will remain CEO while the investigation continues, which will involve independent directors and independent counsel. Nvidia added that it doesn't believe the affair compromised any national security or Nvidia secrets.

Nvidia has been a giant in the video game space for decades, but in recent years, the graphics card manufacturer has evolved into one of the most important links in the US's artificial intelligence chain. The company has profited massively from the growing AI sector, which has driven the prices of vital components to skyrocket. This has had a knock-on effect on gaming hardware like graphics cards and consoles, which in turn have seen prices hit record highs due to rising memory costs.

At the same time, the US under the Trump administration has introduced several new policies to limit China's access to those vital components, with Nvidia emerging as one of the biggest players in the AI arms race.

Following the US midterm elections last week, Nvidia's market cap was reduced by more than $1 trillion, although it did start to rebound later in the trading day--even if the company is being beaten by Krispy Kreme when it comes to overall growth in 2026.

#3662. Let’s Throw “Maxxing” Into the Dustbin of History

There was a land of Usenet forums and AOL keywords, LiveJournals and Blogspots and single-topic Tumblrs. It was called the internet, and it was a patchwork quilt sewn together by delightful little freaks—a collective fabric woven from psychologically damaged but individually discernible threads.

With time, that changed. “It had also once been the place where you sounded like yourself,” Patricia Lockwood, poet laureate of the terminally online, wrote of the internet in her wonderfully bizarre 2021 novel No One Is Talking About This. “Gradually it had become the place where we sounded like each other.”

Never has that been truer than in the wee months of 2026, when everyone suddenly woke up, unlocked their glowing rectangles, and decided to start talking like supplement-addled bridge trolls. Mogging, gooning, bonesmashing, mewing: Without rhyme, reason, or the public’s consent (funny thing about that!), incel language had fully colonized our speech. And after the takeover, no neologism was more prominent than the all-purpose suffix “-maxxing.”

We were not talking about what Cher Horowitz might do with her father’s credit card. We were using a slangier term for optimization, attaching it willy-nilly to any nouns or verbs it could plausibly describe. Working out became gymmaxxing; eating too many beans became fibermaxxing; neglecting to look at your phone for eight whole hours became sleepmaxxing. Like all good colloquialisms, the word was adaptable and edgy and undeniably fun to say. It’s got those playful and lightly pornographic double x’s, the push-pull of a hard k sound—famously the most inherently funny consonant—followed by soft sibilance and a literal “zing.”

But after a full 12 months of maxxing, I am more than ready to minn. And not least because no amount of overuse can obscure the ugly origin of 2026’s favorite syntaxx.

Back in the Gamergate era, maxxing was coined by pathetic losers on websites with names like SlutHate, where they used it to describe how they were hoping to attract women: enhancing their appearances through looksmaxxing, enhancing their social status by moneymaxxing. (Perhaps they could have started by showermaxxing.)

True, innumerable everyday expressions have uncomfortable connotations. Just ask anyone who’s absentmindedly used one of them before pausing to frantically google “Is ‘gung ho’ racist?” (answer: yes, but not in the way you might think) or “butthurt word homophobic??” (fortunately, it’s actually not). But most of those questionable expressions weren’t invented five minutes ago. It’s reasonable to expect the hoi polloi not to know the roots of words that have been grandfathered into the lexicon. Maxxing’s upsetting genesis, though, is easily traceable—and anyone who’s online enough to use it is also probably well-informed enough to know better. (Incidentally, “grandfathered in”? Also racist!)

And then, of course, there’s the death knell of all slang: repetition and co-option by both corporations and figurative bad actors. The fun was over the moment the Cheesecake Factory’s official Instagram account advised its 1.1 million followers to try “brown bread-maxxing.” It was ready for last rites by the time Trump’s Department of Homeland Security tweeted about its intention to engage in “deportationmaxing.” (Yes, with one x; given who authors these posts, you’d think they could have spelled it right.) And it was really in the ground two days after that, when The Wall Street Journal’s X account published this sentence: “The era of AI ‘tokenmaxxing’ in corporate America is over. Companies are now embracing ‘thrift-maxxing.’” At this point, we are dead horse–maxxing every time we insert the term into a new sentence, even—especially—if we’re trying to use it ironically.

Language is contagious, particularly for those who live online. In No One Is Talking About This, Lockwood bemoans internet-speak’s unparalleled ability to infect its users: “It was so tiring to have to catch each new virus, produce the perfect sneeze of it, and then mutate it into something new.” But here’s the thing: Protective measures can be taken. If your phone still autocorrects this particular word to “max inc,” there is hope. The bad news, of course, is that by the time you read this, it’s entirely possible an even worse word will have clawed out of the dark web to take its place.

#3661. Mortal Kombat 2 Is Winning The Race To Become Mortal Kombat 2

What's in a name? That's the question that Mortal Kombat studio CCO Ed Boon is asking, as he recently set up a few polls asking for opinions on what the next Mortal Kombat game should be called. According to Boon, three possible names were on the table: Mortal Kombat 12, Mortal Kombat 13, or Mortal Kombat 2.

"Footnote: Some people are assuming the title with the most votes will determine where we take the story," Boon wrote online. "That’s not the case. We’ve just had difficulty kounting lately."

The current naming convention for Mortal Kombat doesn't make much sense if you've taken a break from the franchise. The series made a successful comeback in 2011 with Mortal Kombat, the ninth installment in the franchise. This was followed by Mortal Kombat X in 2015 and Mortal Kombat 11 in 2019, which brought the original storyline that began in 1992's Mortal Kombat to a close. This was followed by a soft reboot in 2023 with Mortal Kombat 1, which remixed established story beats and put familiar characters in new roles.

To make things even more confusing, Mortal Kombat 1 heavily references multiple timelines toward the end of its campaign, drawing in characters from across a Mortal Kombat multiverse for a final showdown against Shang Tsung from the previous timeline. The Khaos Reigns expansion would also touch on these ideas, as the Titan version of Havik sought to merge all timelines into one.

Currently, "Mortal Kombat 2" is leading the votes with 45.2% of people polled by Boon favoring that title, at the time of writing. If this becomes the title of the next Mortal Kombat game, it will be the second Mortal Kombat 2, which will probably confuse anyone who hasn't been following along. While it hasn't been officially revealed yet, Boon did confirm that Mortal Kombat developer NetherRealm Studios is "pursuing another Mortal Kombat game," and he added that "other forms of media and whatnot" for the Mortal Kombat franchise are in development.

That was back in May, and since then, Mortal Kombat's parent company, Warner Bros. Interactive, has seen some big changes. Paramount’s $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery eventually went through, leading to the merger between Warner Bros. Interactive and Paramount Games Studio. That new entity puts Mortal Kombat, Game of Thrones, Batman, and a treasure trove of IP under the same roof as Avatar: The Last Airbender, South Park, and Star Trek. Tony Driscoll, president of games and experiences at Skydance, will oversee the new division.

India’s most expensive movie ever is Ramayana, which is one of the latest 2026 movie releases to hit theaters. The movie was a massive undertaking, and that's evident just by watching the trailer. All in all, the film is firmly steeped in the culture its representing. But, even though the flick was made thousands of miles from Hollywood, a producer was very much inspired by one of our greatest filmmakers, Christopher Nolan, as CinemaBlend recently learned.

Did you know that Ramayana is co-composed by Hans Zimmer? The German musician has become one of the most beloved and prolific composers of modern cinema, and that’s exactly why the movie's producer, Namit Malhotra, asked for him to come aboard the filmmaking team. Here’s how he told us the story during CB’s exclusive Ramayana interview:

I grew up in India completely fanboying on A.R. Rahman, who I absolutely love and his music has sort of formed a big part of my growing up and childhood and youth. And then, I moved to L.A. in 2010, the year Inception came out. I started to fall in love with Chris Nolan and Han Zimmer's music that was done for The Dark Knight and all the films that came subsequent to that. And, it was one of those moments when we decided to make Ramayana. I said literally as a fanboy, ‘What if I could take Han Zimmer and A.R. Rahman together and they would create a new sound, a new feeling, a new energy that the world has not heard before?’ And everybody is like, ‘Yeah, why not?’

Malhotra called himself a self-described “fanboy” of Nolan movies who's been in awe of his movies for a while. So, when he went on to make his own epic, he thought he'd take the long-shot move to try to get Zimmer on board for Ramayana alongside his favorite composer from India, A.R. Rahman. (Did you know Zimmer actually helped convince Nolan to make Interstellar, by the way? A greatly overlooked detail is just how important musicians like him are pivotal to the filmmaking process.) As Malhotra added:

One thing I learned in America, there's no harm in asking because the worst you'll be told is ‘No’. That's not how we grew up in India. Like you normally don't ask the question if you think the answer is no.

Even though Namit Malhotra had never met Zimmer and didn't know would react to the request, the producer took “a cue from [his] American friends” and reached out to the Interstellar composer. This is what happened next:

I made a pitch and a presentation to him. I couldn't have been more surprised by his intellect, his intuitive judgment because he was like, ‘Namit, you don't have to sell me on Ramayana. If something has existed in the world for over 5,000 years and generation after generation, more people are excited to consume it, learn from it, and it's still not lost its relevance, there must be more than what you and I can understand. So we should just figure out how we do this and not worry about whether we should do it.’

Ramayana Is Making A Huge Global Push. I Still Can't Tell From Reviews What I'm Getting Into

The idea really does sell itself, doesn’t it? Ramayana is a Hindu epic poem that’s very central to India’s culture. It has inspired the celebrations of Diwali and Dussehra, and the story also serves as a moral cornerstone as well. It focuses on two characters: Rama and Ravana. Prince Rama is the seventh incarnation / avatar of Lord Vishnu, who becomes responsible for taking down King Ravana from having uncontrollable power over people. It's India's own classic good vs. evil story, and it has really stood the test of time.

I'm no sure how aware Zimmer was of the legend of Ramayana before it was pitched to him, yet he was apparently sold quite quickly. He got the importance of it being told for the big screen. Malhotra told us that Zimmer’s reaction to his pitch even “revalidated” his own reasons to make it and “reinvigorated [his] own confidence” since he respects the composer so much.

Hans Zimmer is a busy musical savant, who’s recently worked on the Dune movies and the upcoming Harry Potter TV series, so he could have easily passed, but he clearly didn’t want to. And, as a result of his participation, one of Hollywood's best got to put his mark on a historical Indian film. You can hear Zimmer’s original music for Ramayana, which is playing in theaters around the world right now.

Now she's into covering YA television and movies, and plenty of horror. Word webslinger. All her writing should be read in Sarah Connor’s Terminator 2 voice over.

At long last, you can now install Grand Theft Auto 6 on your console via preloading, or at least you can if you live in Australia or New Zealand. Preloading begins in all regions at midnight local time, so people in the US are almost there.

With preloading now live, people have dug through the files and found things they weren't intended to see. That includes references to things like "join Session," "launch Activity," and "launch Multiplayer Activity." People are taking these to be references to a new form of GTA Online.

Rockstar has said GTA 6 is a single-player game, but it’s expected to add some form of online multiplayer at some point. Just because "Multiplayer" was found in the game's files, that doesn't necessarily mean online functionality will be available at launch--it's likely coming sometime later.

People have theorized that GTA 6's story and Online could be separate games. That remains to be seen, but those who have the game preloaded have discovered that GTA 6's "Story" is an individual download within the game's files. Whatever the case, experts and insiders believe GTA 6's new online experience will launch at some point in 2027.

Additionally, the datamining effort led to some discoveries about what Rockstar might be cooking up in terms of PS5 Pro support. People believe they found references to 120Hz support on PS5 Pro, along with multi-frame super resolution, which is known as PSSR on PS5 Pro.

Rockstar has yet to announce any specifics about GTA 6 for PS5 Pro, and the game's trailers so far have been captured on a standard PS5.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. For more, check out the exact worldwide launch times.
